entities.summary:
The Battle of Lesnaya was a pivotal event in the Great Northern War, fought between the Russian Empire and the Swedish Empire on October 9, 1708, in Liasnaja, Russia. The battle saw the Russian forces led by Boris Sheremetev clash with the Swedish army led by Adam Ludwig Lewenhaupt.


The Battle of Lesnaya was a significant turning point in the Great Northern War, as it marked a crucial Russian victory that shifted the balance of power in favor of the Russian Empire. The battle also had far-reaching consequences for the region, leading to the eventual Russian occupation of Livonia and the annexation of Estonia.


The legacy of the Battle of Lesnaya can be seen in the subsequent Russian expansion in Eastern Europe, which had a profound impact on the regional politics and culture. The battle also marked a significant milestone in the rise of the Russian Empire as a major European power.


As historian Adam Zamoyski noted, 'The Battle of Lesnaya was a decisive victory for the Russian Empire, marking the beginning of a new era of Russian dominance in Eastern Europe.'
